newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares climb steeply at close, OTCs rise.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares climb steeply at close, OTCs rise.

text.p: Singapore shares ended higher on Monday with sharp rises in Malaysian over-the counter stocks dominating trade.
"The Malaysian market has already touched its bottom. I expect the market to run in no less than six weeks," said a dealer with a local brokerage.
The UOB OTC index tracking mainly Malaysian stocks rose 10.66 points to 1,184.60.
Dealers said Friday's strong close on Wall Street also boosted selected blue chips and index stocks. The key Straits Times Industrials Index soared 28.22 points to end at 2,154.49.
Positive sentiment was reflected in 247 advancing issues thumping 86 decliners. Market volume was moderate at 131.11 million shares changing hands.
Favourite index stocks Cycle & Carriage, Fraser & Neave and Cerebos were all up between Singapore 70 and 30 cents.
Seaview Hotel surged S$1.40 to S$15.00 on speculation over the redevelopment potential of its site.

Malaysia's Idris Hydraulic was top volume, gaining S$0.09 to S$1.87 with 4.72 million shares traded. A popular speculative stock, Sri Hartamas, also rose S$0.03 to S$1.04 on a turnover of 4.07 million shares. --Seah Beng Nah (65 8703080)
